Numerical data and plots of SISO systems

Source: R/physics-control-plots.R
pole_zero_numerical_data.Rd

pole_zero_numerical_data(system) gives the zeros and the poles of a SISO system. impulse_response_numerical_data(), step_response_numerical_data() and ramp_response_numerical_data() sample the impulse, unit step and ramp responses on n equally spaced times; bode_magnitude_numerical_data() and bode_phase_numerical_data() sample the magnitude (dB) and the phase on n logarithmically spaced frequencies. nyquist_plot_expr() and nichols_plot_expr() give the expressions of the Nyquist and Nichols plots. The *_plot() functions draw the plots with base R graphics. After sympy.physics.control.control_plots.

Usage

pole_zero_numerical_data(system)

impulse_response_numerical_data(
  system,
  prec = 8L,
  lower_limit = 0L,
  upper_limit = 10L,
  n = 1000L,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  ...
)

step_response_numerical_data(
  system,
  prec = 8L,
  lower_limit = 0L,
  upper_limit = 10L,
  n = 1000L,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  ...
)

ramp_response_numerical_data(
  system,
  slope = 1L,
  prec = 8L,
  lower_limit = 0L,
  upper_limit = 10L,
  n = 1000L,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  ...
)

bode_magnitude_numerical_data(
  system,
  initial_exp = -5L,
  final_exp = 5L,
  freq_unit = "rad/sec",
  n = 1000L,
  ...
)

bode_phase_numerical_data(
  system,
  initial_exp = -5L,
  final_exp = 5L,
  freq_unit = "rad/sec",
  phase_unit = "rad",
  phase_unwrap = TRUE,
  n = 1000L,
  ...
)

nyquist_plot_expr(system)

nichols_plot_expr(system)

pole_zero_plot(
  system,
  pole_color = "blue",
  pole_markersize = 10,
  zero_color = "orange",
  zero_markersize = 7,
  grid = TRUE,
  show_axes = TRUE,
  show = TRUE,
  ...
)

step_response_plot(
  system,
  color = "blue",
  prec = 8L,
  lower_limit = 0L,
  upper_limit = 10L,
  show_axes = FALSE,
  grid = TRUE,
  show = TRUE,
  ...
)

impulse_response_plot(
  system,
  color = "blue",
  prec = 8L,
  lower_limit = 0L,
  upper_limit = 10L,
  show_axes = FALSE,
  grid = TRUE,
  show = TRUE,
  ...
)

ramp_response_plot(
  system,
  slope = 1L,
  color = "blue",
  prec = 8L,
  lower_limit = 0L,
  upper_limit = 10L,
  show_axes = FALSE,
  grid = TRUE,
  show = TRUE,
  ...
)

bode_magnitude_plot(
  system,
  initial_exp = -5L,
  final_exp = 5L,
  color = "blue",
  show_axes = FALSE,
  grid = TRUE,
  show = TRUE,
  freq_unit = "rad/sec",
  ...
)

bode_phase_plot(
  system,
  initial_exp = -5L,
  final_exp = 5L,
  color = "blue",
  show_axes = FALSE,
  grid = TRUE,
  show = TRUE,
  freq_unit = "rad/sec",
  phase_unit = "rad",
  phase_unwrap = TRUE,
  ...
)

bode_plot(
  system,
  initial_exp = -5L,
  final_exp = 5L,
  grid = TRUE,
  show_axes = FALSE,
  show = TRUE,
  freq_unit = "rad/sec",
  phase_unit = "rad",
  phase_unwrap = TRUE,
  ...
)

nyquist_plot(
  system,
  initial_omega = 0.01,
  final_omega = 100,
  show = TRUE,
  color = "blue",
  n = 1000L,
  ...
)

nichols_plot(
  system,
  initial_omega = 0.01,
  final_omega = 100,
  show = TRUE,
  color = "blue",
  n = 1000L,
  ...
)

Arguments

system

A SISO system.

prec

The precision of the evaluation (kept for compatibility).

lower_limit, upper_limit

The time range.

n

The number of points.

adaptive

Ignored; the points are always equally spaced.

...

Further arguments.

slope

The slope of the ramp.

initial_exp, final_exp

The frequency range as powers of ten.

freq_unit

"rad/sec" or "Hz".

phase_unit

"rad" or "deg".

phase_unwrap

Whether to unwrap the phase.

pole_markersize, zero_markersize

The marker sizes.

grid, show_axes, show

Whether to draw a grid, the axes, and the plot.

color, pole_color, zero_color

The colors.

initial_omega, final_omega

The frequency range of the Nyquist and Nichols plots.

Value

A list of the x and y values (pole_zero_numerical_data(): of the zeros and poles), a list of expressions, or, for the plots, the data invisibly.

Examples

s <- Symbol("s")
G <- TransferFunction(1, s^2 + s + 1, s)
pole_zero_numerical_data(G)
#> ([], [-0.5-0.8660254i, -0.5+0.8660254i]) 
step_response_numerical_data(G, n = 5)
#> [[1]]
#> [1]  0.0  2.5  5.0  7.5 10.0
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 0.0000000 1.0233596 1.0745906 0.9741517 1.0021701
#>
